Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) shows a large, well-defined opacity in the right upper lung. The CT scan (Figure 2) confirms a large, homogenous mass with smooth margins that displaces adjacent structures but does not appear to invade vessels or the diaphragm (which is at a normal level). The MRI images (Figures 3 and 4) further support the finding of a well-circumscribed, homogenous mass without signs of local invasion.
